resources.string: Tutorial
Welcome to Space Compass
Explore the sky, follow celestial paths and preview other places and times. Discover the main controls with the interactive tutorial.
Touch a highlighted control or an orbit point to learn what it does.
Zoom
Selected object
Orbit points
Open app information, release notes and source credits.
Open settings, saved scenes and the tutorial.
Choose the objects to display. Search, filter and save favorites in the catalog.
Preview another position, altitude, time zone, date or time, and adjust how time advances.
Choose the grid, its numbers and planetary lines, then Apply.
0–24 shows the calendar day; +24h shows 24 hours from the displayed time.
Choose a mode and view, then Apply. Close keeps your current choices.
Show or hide weather effects in the simulated sky and panoramas.
Choose the camera axis (90°) or the phone length axis (0°) for pointing.
Make object images more translucent to compare them with the camera view.
Zoom in or out with this button or two fingers.
Prepare an image. In the preview, choose grid, labels and position; in Sky and Globe, switch between Framed view and Panorama.
Collapse or expand the object and compass islands to gain sky space.
Tap to show or hide antipodes. Hold to deselect all points.
Move through the selected objects. The island shows the active object and its trajectory colors.
Open object data, paths, key heights, events and personal moments.
Open the active object’s trajectory, times, elevations and selectable points. Future events can have reminders.
Open details of your real position, GPS altitude, orientation and weather. These values are independent of the Location.
Select or deselect a point. Aim the reticle to read time, T, azimuth and elevation.
Time and interface
Tap empty space to pause or resume time. Double-tap to hide or show the interface and panels.
Open Android’s alarm or calendar for an eligible future event. Past events and the current point cannot have an alarm.
Status and recovery
Check status and available actions for position, weather and orbital data.
Remove the active object from the selected objects after confirmation.
